intro.caption: Lesson 5-9 — area of regular polygons. The Cubeland Build-Off finals need a brand-new Hex Arena floor, and one wrong triangle will ruin the turf order!

balloons.t: We need turf for this whole six-sided arena! How do we find a regular polygon's area?
Slice it like a giant six-slice pizza!
A hexagon splits into four triangles! I already ordered four slices of turf!
Draw lines from the CENTER to every corner! Six sides make SIX equal triangles!

pages.caption: When you decompose a regular polygon from its center, the number of congruent triangles always equals the number of sides.

balloons.t: Every side of the polygon becomes the base of one center triangle!
Each triangle uses ½ × base × height. The polygon's side is the base!
And the distance from the center to the side is the height. Don't skip the ½!
Pentagons have 5 triangles, octagons have 8. Multiply one triangle by the side count!
Got it! One triangle times how many sides—never stop after just one!
Too bad! You'll probably forget the ½ or use 4 triangles on a hexagon!
Six triangles, one area, times six, times the turf cost. Watch us!
261 square feet of turf! Hex Arena is open for business!

win.caption: To find the area of any regular polygon, decompose it from the center into congruent triangles, find one triangle (½ × base × height), and multiply by the number of sides.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Count the Triangles
gates.prompt: Draw lines from the center to each corner of a regular polygon. How many congruent triangles form?
hints: Conceptual: every side of the regular polygon forms the outer base of one triangle meeting at the center.
Procedural: count the sides of the polygon—that is the exact number of center triangles.

steps: Practice shape: a regular pentagon has 5 equal sides and 5 corners.
Drawing lines from the center to each of the 5 corners splits it into 5 equal triangles.
worked.q: How many center triangles does a regular square split into?

items.q: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides. How many congruent triangles form when you draw lines from the center to each corner?

options.fb: 6 triangles is a hexagon (6 sides). An octagon has 8 sides.
Each side makes one triangle to the center, so 8 sides make 8 triangles.
You don't double the sides—there is 1 center triangle per side.

items.q: Dree says a regular hexagon splits from the center into 4 triangles. Why is that wrong?

options.t: Each of the 6 sides is the base of one triangle, so there are 6 triangles

options.fb: A hexagon has 6 sides and 6 corners.

options.t: You have to double the number of sides to get 12 triangles
options.fb: Lines from the center to the 6 corners make 6 triangles, not 12.

gates.pass: Sides equal center triangles! Dree cancels her 4-slice order.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Area of One Triangle
gates.prompt: Find the area of just ONE center triangle using ½ × base × height. (Nonsquare heights are rounded.)
hints: Conceptual: a triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height.
Procedural: multiply the side length (base) by the triangle's height, then take half.

steps: Practice triangle: base = 6 ft, height ≈ 5.2 ft.
worked.q: One center triangle has base 10 ft and height 5 ft. What is its area?

items.label: A hexagon's center triangle has base 8 ft and height 7 ft. Area of ONE triangle (sq ft):
items.aria: area of one triangle with base 8 and height 7 in square feet

fb.msg: 56 is 8 × 7. A triangle's area is HALF of base × height!
168 is all 6 triangles combined! This step asks for just ONE triangle.

items.label: A pentagon's center triangle has base 4 in and height 2.8 in. Area of ONE triangle (sq in):
items.aria: area of one triangle with base 4 and height 2.8 in square inches

fb.msg: 11.2 forgot the ½ (4 × 2.8). Take half for a triangle.
28 is the whole 5-triangle pentagon! This asks for just ONE triangle.

gates.pass: 28 sq ft and 5.6 sq in! Kai locks in the triangle rule.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Total Area
gates.prompt: Now multiply ONE triangle's area by the number of triangles to get the total area of the regular polygon.
hints: Conceptual: all center triangles in a regular polygon are congruent (identical).
Procedural: find one triangle's area, then multiply by the number of sides.

steps: Practice pentagon: 5 triangles, each with base 6 ft and height 4 ft.
worked.q: A regular square has 4 center triangles, each 9 sq ft. Total area?

items.label: A regular hexagon tile has 6 triangles, each 12 cm². Total tile area (cm²):
items.aria: total area of regular hexagon with 6 triangles of 12 square centimeters

fb.msg: 12 cm² is only 1 triangle. A hexagon has 6 of them!
48 is 4 × 12. A hexagon has 6 sides, not 4.

items.label: A regular octagon gazebo has 8 triangles, each base 5 ft and height 6 ft. Total area (sq ft):
items.aria: total area of regular octagon with base 5 and height 6

fb.msg: 15 sq ft is only 1 triangle. Multiply by all 8 triangles.
240 forgot ½ on each triangle (8 × 30). One triangle is ½ × 5 × 6 = 15.
90 is 6 × 15. An octagon has 8 triangles, not 6!

items.fbDefault: Find one triangle (½ × 5 × 6 = 15), then multiply by 8.

gates.pass: 72 cm² and 120 sq ft! Moss stacks the pentagon and octagon tiles.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Plan the Seats
gates.prompt: Finish the main Hex Arena floor! Each side is 10 ft, and each center triangle has height 8.7 ft.
hints: Conceptual: decompose the hexagon into 6 congruent triangles, find the total area, then multiply by the cost per sq ft.
Procedural: 1) ½ × 10 × 8.7 for one triangle; 2) multiply by 6 for total sq ft; 3) multiply by $2.

steps: Practice plaza: regular pentagon (5 sides), base 4 ft, height 3 ft.
One triangle = ½ × 4 × 3 = 6 sq ft. Total = 5 × 6 = 30 sq ft.
worked.q: If a 40 sq ft floor costs $3 per sq ft, what is the cost?

items.label: Step 1 · Hex Arena side = 10 ft, triangle height = 8.7 ft. Area of ONE triangle (sq ft):
items.aria: area of one center triangle of Hex Arena in square feet

fb.msg: 87 is 10 × 8.7. Take half for a triangle: ½ × 87.

items.label: Step 2 · Total area of all 6 triangles of the Hex Arena (sq ft):
items.aria: total area of six triangles of Hex Arena in square feet

fb.msg: 522 forgot ½ on the triangles (6 × 87). Multiply 6 × 43.5.
43.5 is only 1 triangle. Multiply by all 6 triangles.
174 is 4 × 43.5. A hexagon has 6 triangles, not 4!

items.label: Step 3 · Turf tiles cost $2 per sq ft. Total cost for 261 sq ft ($):
items.aria: total cost in dollars for 261 square feet at 2 dollars each

fb.msg: 263 is 261 + 2. Multiply 261 sq ft by $2 per sq ft.

gates.pass: ROAR! 43.5 sq ft per slice, 261 sq ft total, $522! The Hex Arena gleams bright green.

journal.heading: Lesson 5-9 — what the arena taught us
rows: Lines from the center to every corner split a regular polygon into congruent triangles—one triangle per side.
Use A = ½ × base × height, where the polygon's side is the base and the center-to-side distance is the height.
Total area = (area of one triangle) × (number of sides).
A hexagon has 6 sides, so it makes 6 center triangles—never 4. And never forget the ½!
journal.quote: "Count the sides, find one slice, multiply—and keep Gel off the wet turf." — Moss

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 5-9 (Area of Regular Polygons) as one focused read. Covers only this lesson: decomposing regular polygons from the center into congruent triangles, finding one triangle's area (½bh), and multiplying by the number of sides.
standards: Derive and apply formulas for areas of triangles, quadrilaterals, and polygons by decomposing into triangles and rectangles
